messages.author: 50e3f32525c093d1
messages.subject: Error in nimbleRcall
parts:
Hi All,

From the NIMBLE manual 0.8.0, under 11.7, it says that I can try to call uncompiled R function from complied nimbleFunctions. Hence, I would like to try to call the function "approx" in R (under the stats package). Heres my attempt at calling it:


myapprox <- function(x,y,xout){approx(x,y,xout)$y}

myapproxR <- nimbleRcall(function(x = double(100000),y = double(100000), 
                                  xout = double(1)){}, 
                                  Rfun = 'myapprox',
                                  returnType = double(1))

samplerData <- list(obsy = obsy    # Response variable
)

samplerConst <- list(N = N, # Sample size
                     Nre = Nre, 
                     re = re, # This is used to "iterate"
                     erry = erry,
                     syst = syst,
                     obsx = obsx,   # Predictors
                     interp.x = interp.x,
                     interp.y = interp.y
)

samplerInits <- list(a.scale = 1,
                     y.norm = rep(1,Nre),
                     y.scat = rep(0.01,Nre),
                     mt = 0,
                     ya = approx(x = interp.x,y = interp.y,xout=obsx)
)


I then proceed to create a nimbleModel but this error pops up:


defining model...
Error in replaceConstantsRecurse(x, constEnv, constNames) : 
  Error, hit end
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In replaceConstantsRecurse(x, constEnv, constNames) :
  Code interp.x was given as known but evaluates to a non-scalar.  This is probably not what you want.
2: In replaceConstantsRecurse(x, constEnv, constNames) :
  Code interp.y was given as known but evaluates to a non-scalar.  This is probably not what you want.

How do I go around resolving this error?

Furthermore, according to the manual in 11.2.3, most of the function under math and linear algebra seems to be working except for interp.lin(x,v1,v2). I tried to replace this using the R's approx function but faced an error in the end. Are there any alternatives to this function? Or should I rewrite the function in NIMBLE from scratch under nimbleFunction? Thanks!

HK Tan (Hong Kiat Tan),
Undergraduate Student | Physics 
National University of Singapore

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Error in nimbleRcall
parts:
Hi HK,

In the type declaration system, "double(D)" means there will be D indices.  If you want a vector of length 100000, you would use "x = double(1)" to indicate x will be one-dimensional in the sense of taking one index.  If xout is also a vector then "xout = double(1)" is correct.  But if xout is a scalar, you want "xout = double(0)".  The same goes for the returnType.  You haven't shown how you are trying to use myapproxR, so I can't tell what you intend.

As you note, another option would be to write what you need as a nimbleFunction, which will give faster performance.

-Perry

################
# Nimble Function, myapprox
###############
# E is in MeV, S is in eV b; convert to MeV and MeV b, respectively
theory <- read.table("Marcucci2005.dat", header=FALSE)

interp.x <- theory[,1] 
interp.y <- theory[,2]*1e-6
len <- length(interp.x)
yainit <- approx(x = interp.x,y = interp.y,xout=obsx)

myapproxR <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(x = double(1,100000),y=double(1,100000),xout =double(0)){
    ind <- max(which(xout>x))
    ans <- (y[ind+1]-y[ind])/(x[ind+1]-x[ind])*(xout-x[ind])
    return(ans)
    returnType(double(0))
  }
)

samplerCode <-  nimbleCode({
  for (i in 1:N) {
    obsy[i] ~ dnorm(ya[i], sd = erry[i])
    # Propagating the errors in observations of y
    ya[i] ~ dnorm(y.norm[re[i]]*mut[i],sd = y.scat[re[i]])
    # Temp mean (mut) multiplied by normalising constant, 
    # re[i] refers to the index that we would use to refer to the category
    mut[i] <- a.scale*myapproxR(interp.x,interp.y,obsx[i])
    # Interpolate and scale
  }
  
  ## PRIORS
  # Scaling factor of theory 
  a.scale ~ T(dnorm(0, pow(5,-2)),0,Inf)  
  
  for (k in 1:Nre){
    # Systematic Uncertainty as a highly informative prior
    y.norm[k] ~ dlnorm(log(1.0),sd=syst[k])
    y.scat[k] ~  T(dnorm(mt, sd=5),0,Inf)
  }
  mt ~  T(dnorm(0, sd=5),0,Inf) # Hyperprior

})

samplerData <- list(obsy = obsy    # Response variable
)

samplerConst <- list(N = N, # Sample size
                     Nre = Nre, 
                     re = re, # This is used to "iterate"
                     erry = erry,
                     syst = syst,
                     obsx = obsx,   # Predictors
                     interp.x = interp.x,
                     interp.y = interp.y
)

samplerInits <- list(a.scale = 1,
                     y.norm = rep(1,Nre),
                     y.scat = rep(0.01,Nre),
                     mt = 0,

ya = yainit
)
# Here, we are using the R's version of approx <-> interp.lin in JAGS

# All the sampled parameters have to the FULLY SPECIFIED

n.chains = 3
n.iter = 75000
n.burnin = 10000

mcmc.out <- nimbleMCMC(code = samplerCode, constants = samplerConst,
                       data = samplerData, inits = samplerInits,
                       nchains = n.chains, 
                       niter = n.iter,
                       nburnin = n.burnin,
                       summary = TRUE, WAIC = TRUE,
                       monitors = c('a.scale',
                                    'y.norm','y.scat')
)

The same error persisted. However, I've realized that I could actually do the approx outside of NIMBLE and set the output of the approx to be the new constants (to replace obsx) and I've tried it on a simple example and it works! Was just wondering if I could actually use myapproxR in NIMBLE (in the case whereby I would have to really use the function in NIMBLE). Thanks!

HK Tan (Hong Kiat Tan),
Undergraduate Student | Physics 
National University of Singapore

Hi HK,

The first line of your code reads a table from file, so I can't reproduce your case and check if I can fix it.

One problem is that you need to provide indexing brackets in non-scalars in model code:

mut[i] <- a.scale*myapproxR(interp.x[],interp.y[],obsx[i])

or 

mut[i] <- a.scale*myapproxR(interp.x[1:10000],interp.y[1:10000],obsx[i]) 

Responses may be limited for the rest of this week.
